extractedText: KT to Expand 'AI for All' Consortium Beyond 20 Partners■ 'Eum Inside' Press Briefing Expansion Under Review From 16 Current Members to More Than 20 In-House GPUs Secured for Stable Operation "Paid Tiers Possible for Business and Premium Services"Finance|Published 2026.09.13. 09:45:03| Updated 2026.09.13. 18:06:59|By Cho Yoon-jinjo@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAALee Jin-hyung, head of KT's AI transformation (AX) business division, explains the "AI for All" service to be developed by the KT consortium on Nov. 11. Photo courtesy of KTLee Jin-hyung, head of KT's AI transformation (AX) business division, explains the "AI for All" service to be developed by the KT consortium on Nov. 11. Photo courtesy of KTKT plans to expand its "AI for All" consortium, currently made up of 16 companies including Zigbang, Daum and Musinsa, and is reviewing whether to introduce paid services if needed to keep the platform running smoothly.Lee Jin-hyung, head of KT's AI Transformation (AX) business division, said at an online press briefing on Sept. 11 that the company is "reviewing a plan to increase the AI for All consortium from the current 16 members to more than 20." Lee said seven additional companies, including major domestic financial groups and hotel and restaurant reservation service providers, have asked to join as partners. "We are reviewing additional partnerships with these companies and will continue to accept applications from others," Lee said.KT had earlier unveiled "Eum Inside," a service that links a general-purpose AI agent based on real-time search with specialized AI services across more than 10 fields including public administration, education, finance and shopping. The consortium currently includes Upstage, Saltlux, Daum, Musinsa, EBS and BC Card, and KT appears to have concluded that more partners are needed to deliver such a range of services.A KT official said the company will "build the AI for All application into a core platform for public use of AI, and apply AI for All features to the Daum search portal, the various service touchpoints of consortium members and KT's Genie TV using the Eum Inside strategy." The official added that users "will be able to enjoy the same AI experience naturally within the services they already use, without having to install a separate app."For example, once Eum Inside is applied to Zigbang, a consortium member, the AI would deliver information such as: "A new recorded sale price has come out for the apartment you're looking at," "Of the 11 listings in this complex, two are below market price," and "It's 50 million won below yesterday's recorded sale price and was listed only two days ago."In the public sector, KT plans to implement AI agent services tailored to each user's circumstances, going beyond simple question-and-answer to offer proactive alerts and personalized benefit recommendations. Public alerts, public benefits matched to age and place of residence, conversational guidance through administrative procedures, and support for issuing and applying for documents are all expected to run within the Eum app and website. A KT official said the company will "expand the service into more areas such as farming and startups, and draw new companies into the business to upgrade it into an AI agent service that directly supports people's daily lives."These services run on Token Factory, KT's AI operating platform. KT plans to integrate a range of domestically developed AI models including Solar, Motif and Mi:dm, along with Rebellions' neural processing units (NPUs) and infrastructure optimization technology from Lablup and Vessl AI, and operate them together on Token Factory to automatically connect the optimal AI model for each service and deliver stable AI services.Token Factory separates the processing of user prompts from response generation and allocates resources optimized for each stage, improving tokens per minute (TPM) by about 31%. It can also cut input tokens by up to 80% through various prompt compression technologies, raising GPU utilization."To take AI for All seriously, KT has secured additional GPUs on top of those supported by the government," Lee said. "We have a technical buffer of about 20% in case traffic surges, and we also hold GPUs for cases that exceed that."KT has also left open the possibility of charging for some AI for All services. "If the government at some point opens a monetization model to the general public as well, we plan to separate out a premium service for the public and offer it separately," Lee said. "We also have plans to apply a paid model if needed for professional use, particularly the PC version of the AI agent for business, when it launches in January as part of AI for All."#KT#AIforAll#EumInside#TokenFactory#AIagent#KoreaAICompanies in this storyKT Corporation030200.KS · TelecomAI KEY Company Analysis →Original reporting by Cho Yoon-jin for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
